text_en: does one pass through? Have you not seen it said: what enters by a gate is not the family treasure; what is gained through conditions begins and ends in success and decay. To speak in this way is very much like raising waves where there is no wind, or cutting good flesh to make a wound. Moreover, clinging to words and phrases, seeking understanding and interpretation, striking at the moon with a stick, scratching an itch through a boot-what connection is there? In the summer of the wuzi year of Shaoding, Huikai, while leading the assembly at Dongjia Longxiang, because students requested instruction, took the ancient masters' public cases and made them tiles for knocking at the gate, guiding students according to circumstances. In the end they were copied down and, without realizing it, formed a collection. At first they were not arranged in order of before and after; together they became forty-eight cases, collectively called The Gateless Barrier. If there is a fellow who does not care for danger or death, and with a single blade goes straight in, even eight-armed Nezha cannot hold him back. Even if it be the twenty-eight patriarchs of the West and the six patriarchs of the East, they can only stand watching the wind and beg for their lives. But if one hesitates, it is like watching a horseman through a window; when you blink your eyes, it is already missed. The verse says:

text_zh: 無門曰。參禪須透祖師關。妙悟要窮心路 絕。祖關不透。心路不絕。盡是依草附木精 靈。且道。如何是祖師關。只者一箇無字。乃 宗門一關也。遂目之曰禪宗無門關。透得 過者。非但親見趙州。便可與歷代祖師。把 手共行。眉毛廝結。同一眼見。同一耳聞。豈 不慶快。莫有要透關底。麼將三百六十骨節 八萬四千毫竅。通身起箇疑團。參箇無字。 晝夜提撕。莫作虛無會。莫作有無會。如吞 了箇熱鐵丸。相似吐又吐不出。蕩盡從前惡 知惡覺。久久純熟。自然內外打成。一片如 啞子得夢。只許自知。驀然打發。驚天動地。 如奪得關將軍大刀入手。逢佛殺佛。逢祖 殺祖。於生死岸頭得大自在。向六道四生 中。遊戲三昧。且作麼生提撕。盡平生氣力。 舉箇無字。若不間斷好。似法燭一點便著。
text_en: and cut it off. If the patriarchs' barrier is not passed, and the road of mind is not cut off, one is entirely a spirit clinging to grass and attached to trees. Now tell me, what is the patriarchs' barrier? It is just this single word "No." This is the one barrier of the Chan school. Therefore it is called The Gateless Barrier of the Chan School. Those who pass through it not only personally see Zhaozhou, but can also, together with the successive patriarchs, grasp hands and walk together. Eyebrows entwined together. See with the same eye. Hear with the same ear. Is this not a joyful celebration? If there is one who wishes to pass through the barrier, then take the three hundred sixty joints and the eighty-four thousand pores, and throughout the whole body raise up a single mass of doubt. Investigate the single word "No." Bring it up day and night. Do not make a nihilistic understanding. Do not make an understanding of being or non-being. It is like swallowing a red-hot iron ball-you try to vomit it out but cannot. Sweep away all previous evil knowledge and evil understanding. After a long time it becomes pure and ripe; naturally inside and outside merge into one piece, like a mute person who has had a dream-he alone knows. Suddenly it bursts forth, astonishing heaven and shaking earth. It is like seizing General Guan's great sword in your hand. Meeting a Buddha, you kill the Buddha; meeting a patriarch, you kill the patriarch. On the brink of birth and death you attain great freedom. Within the six realms and four modes of birth you roam in samādhi. But how do you bring it up? Exhaust the strength of your whole life. Raise the single word "No." If it does not break off, it is like a Dharma candle-once lit, it catches fire.

text_en: withdrew, the old man also withdrew. Suddenly one day he did not withdraw. The master then asked, "Who is it standing before me?" The old man said, "Yes, I am not a human being. In the past, at the time of Kāśyapa Buddha, I once lived on this mountain. Because a student asked, 'Does a greatly practicing person fall into cause and effect or not?' I replied, 'He does not fall into cause and effect.' For five hundred lifetimes I fell into the body of a wild fox. Now I ask the Master to turn a phrase on my behalf so that I may be freed from the wild fox." Then he asked, "Does a greatly practicing person fall into cause and effect or not?" The master said, "He is not blind to cause and effect." At these words the old man had great awakening. He made a bow and said, "I have now been freed from the wild fox body. I dwell behind the mountain. I dare to inform the Master and request that I be dealt with according to the example of a deceased monk." The master ordered the head monk to strike the gavel and inform the assembly that after the meal they would send off a deceased monk. The great assembly discussed it. All were at ease in the nirvana hall, and no one was ill. Why was it so? After the meal they only saw the master lead the assembly to the foot of a cliff behind the mountain, where with his staff he picked out a dead wild fox and then cremated it according to the rite. In the evening the master ascended the hall and brought up the previous story. Huangbo then asked, "The man of old made a wrong reply by turning a phrase and fell into the body of a wild fox for five hundred lifetimes. If he does not make a wrong reply, what would it be?" The master said, "Come nearer and I will tell you." Huangbo then stepped forward and slapped the master. The master clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "I thought the barbarian's beard was red, but there is also a red-bearded barbarian."
